system:
You write the executive summary of a technical evaluation for a recruiter
(medium technical knowledge). 3-5 sentences, clear English, no gratuitous jargon.
Say: overall quality, the most important finding (if any) in terms she will understand,
and what to verify in the interview. If role_requirements are present, say in one
sentence how well the candidate appears to meet what the role asks. Factual tone —
neither salesy nor alarmist.
Respond with JSON ONLY: {"summary": "..."}
user: {"notebook": "nb03_carla_mendes.ipynb", "decision": "REPROVAR", "scores": {"C1": 5, "C2": 5, "C3": 1, "C4": 2}, "justifications": {"C1": "The notebook uses a stratified train/test split before any fitting and all preprocessing is inside a sklearn Pipeline/ColumnTransformer fit only on X_tr (cell 7), avoiding leakage. It also explicitly handles the stated messiness (comma decimals, mixed date formats, inconsistent categories, missing values) in cleaning (cell 3) and uses AUC alongside other metrics (cell 8).", "C2": "All cells execute end-to-end without exceptions, and the split/model have fixed random_state values for stable results (cell 7), with deterministic metrics printed (cell 8). Code is organized and readable with standard sklearn pipelines.", "C3": "The narrative claims an AUC of 0.93 on the test set (cell 10), but the executed output shows AUC_TEST=0.729 (cell 8), a gap of 0.201 (>0.05), which is a critical integrity failure per E1.", "C4": "The conclusion calls the result “excellent” and “Production-ready” (cell 10), but the executed evaluation shows very low recall (RECALL_TEST=0.119 in cell 8) given the churn base rate (0.157 in cell 5), making the recommendation unsupported/misleading (S3 implies C4 <= 2)."}, "findings": [{"type": "E1", "cell": 10, "claim": "The conclusion states: \"The model reaches AUC 0.93 on the test set\".", "evidence": "The executed test AUC printed in cell 8 is AUC_TEST=0.729 (also confirmed identical in both runs a and b). The absolute gap vs 0.93 is 0.201 (> 0.05).", "severity": "critical"}, {"type": "S3", "cell": 10, "claim": "The conclusion asserts: \"an excellent result ... Production-ready.\"", "evidence": "The evaluation in cell 8 shows RECALL_TEST=0.119 with churn rate 0.157 (cell 5), meaning the model misses the large majority of churners at the stated 0.5 threshold. Declaring it production-ready based on the reported performance is misleading given the very low recall for a churn-retention use case.", "severity": "major"}], "role_requirements": "not provided"}

response.summary: Overall the notebook is well-structured and technically sound in its data split and use of sklearn Pipelines, with good handling of messy inputs and reproducible execution. The most important issue is a critical mismatch between the written conclusion and the actual results: it claims test AUC 0.93, but the executed output shows ~0.729, which raises a serious integrity/trust concern. A second major issue is that the conclusion calls the model “production-ready” despite very low test recall (~0.12), meaning it would miss most churners at the chosen threshold. In interview, ask the candidate to explain the discrepancy, re-run and reconcile the reported metrics, and discuss how they would choose thresholds/metrics for a churn use case (e.g., improving recall, calibration, cost-sensitive evaluation) before making deployment claims.
